title: Part
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with the Euler angles set to zero and the translation vector also set to zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. This sketch consists of a single loop made up of eight curves. The first arc begins at the point [0.0, 0.0035], passes through the midpoint [0.001, 0.001], and ends at [0.0035, 0.0]. Following this, draw the first line from [0.0035, 0.0] to [0.0105, 0.0]. The second arc starts at [0.0105, 0.0], has a midpoint at [0.0129, 0.001], and ends at [0.014, 0.0035]. The second line runs from [0.014, 0.0035] to [0.014, 0.0105]. The third arc begins at [0.014, 0.0105], passes through [0.0129, 0.0129], and ends at [0.0105, 0.014]. The third line connects [0.0105, 0.014] to [0.0035, 0.014]. The fourth arc starts at [0.0035, 0.014], has a midpoint at [0.001, 0.0129], and ends at [0.0, 0.0105]. Finally, the fourth line completes the loop by connecting [0.0, 0.0105] back to [0.0, 0.0035]. After drawing the sketch, apply a scale factor of 0.014 to the entire sketch. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using the Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] and translating it using the translation vector [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Extrude the transformed sketch 0.75 units in the direction of the normal, ensuring that no extrusion occurs in the opposite direction. Integrate this new part with the previous body by creating a new solid body. The final dimensions of the cylindrical object with the small rectangular protrusion at the top are a length of 0.013953488372093023 units, a width of 0.013953488372093023 units, and a height of 0.75 units.

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0035) \
     .threePointArc((0.001, 0.001), (0.0035, 0.0)) \
     .lineTo(0.0105, 0.0) \
     .threePointArc((0.0129, 0.001), (0.014, 0.0035)) \
     .lineTo(0.014, 0.0105) \
     .threePointArc((0.0129, 0.0129), (0.0105, 0.014)) \
     .lineTo(0.0035, 0.014) \
     .threePointArc((0.001, 0.0129), (0.0, 0.0105)) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0035) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the base of the cylinder
sketch = (
    workplane
    .moveTo(0.0, 0.0044)
    .threePointArc((0.0013, 0.0013), (0.0044, 0.0))
    .lineTo(0.0096, 0.0)
    .threePointArc((0.0127, 0.0013), (0.014, 0.0044))
    .lineTo(0.014, 0.0096)
    .threePointArc((0.0127, 0.0127), (0.0096, 0.014))
    .lineTo(0.0044, 0.014)
    .threePointArc((0.0013, 0.0127), (0.0, 0.0096))
    .lineTo(0.0, 0.0044)
    .close()
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.75)

# Assign the final model to 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane object
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the outer profile
r = r.moveTo(0.007, 0).threePointArc((0, 0), (0, 0.007)) \
     .lineTo(0, 0.007).threePointArc((0, 0.014), (0.007, 0.014)) \
     .lineTo(0.007, 0.014).threePointArc((0.014, 0.014), (0.014, 0.007)) \
     .lineTo(0.014, 0.007).threePointArc((0.014, 0), (0.007, 0)).close()

# Extrude the profile
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Cut out the inner profile
r = r.faces('>Z').workplane().moveTo(0.002, 0.002).lineTo(0.012, 0.002).lineTo(0.012, 0.012).lineTo(0.002, 0.012).close().cutBlind(-0.75)
